newsitem.title: ABU DHABI: British Aerospace to invest $20 mln in UAE firm.
newsitem.headline: British Aerospace to invest $20 mln in UAE firm.

text.p: British Aerospace Plc (BA) is expected to invest $20 million in a new $136 million leasing company based in the United Arab Emirates, industry executives said on Sunday.
"British Aerospace will put in $20 million, that is 15 percent of the new firm's paid-up capital. They will put in cold, hard cash," said an executive close to the company.

The sources said al-Waha International Leasing Co will have a 500 million dirham ($136 million) capital, of which 45 percent will be paid in by the founders, with rest coming from an initial public offering in early June. A total of 50 million shares will be issued at 10 dirhams a share.
"The actual capital of the company at the launch will be 500 million dirhams. This is not a paper deal, this is a strategic alliance for the long term," one executive said.

Abu Dhabi state institutions, UAE founders and other Gulf bodies will have a 30 percent share. The founders are led by the UAE Offset Group and Abu Dhabi Investment Company (ADIC) British Aerospace managers, executives said.

UAE member Abu Dhabi on Sunday issued a decree setting up the new company which will seek leasing deals in the oil-rich Gulf region for a variety of high-ticket items like commercial aircraft, ships, heavy machinery and power plants.
The excutives said that BA, like the other founders, is obliged to hold its stake in the new firm for at least two years.

But the British company's interest in the project is for the long-term. It "is an investment which will earn good return, complement our existing business and help a highly important customer add value to the economy", a BA official told Reuters.

The emirate's Abu Dhabi Investment Authority (ADIA) owns about 2.8 percent of British Aerospace which has provided the Gulf state with Hawk warplanes and trainers and other military hardware over the years, industry sources said.
The deal is not part of the UAE's programme to have arms suppliers reinvest a portion of a deal's worth back into the country or a pre-offset for a pending requirement, they added.
BA is among companies bidding for a UAE requirement for up to 80 warplanes possibly worth more than $6 billion.
Abu Dhabi "feels that British Aerospace has a good and strong track record in asset management", one source said.

Abu Dhabi officials have said they expect the leasing concept to appeal to regional states which are trying to cut capital expenditure as their economies gradually recover from the high costs of the 1991 Gulf War and low oil prices.
